details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 9 - The Veterans · Seat 2, Skirmisher

A blonde half-elf duellist in a sea-blue cloak, rapier in one hand and a long parrying dagger at her hip, who learned her footwork on the docks and decks of Opal. Teasing, theatrical and quick to apologise to the foe she has just embarrassed. She joined the Keepers for a steady fee and a good story, and stayed because they are the only crew she trusts at her back.

In a fight

Pick one foe and keep it to yourself for Duel's Rhythm, then hit it again and again for Relentless Assault. Parry the big blows, Riposte the misses, and dance clear with Hit and Run and Acrobatic Escape.
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities (from the printed sheet)

Flourish Manoeuvres. Once a round, out of turn, one of these. Parry: when struck in melee, a Dexterity check (d20+4) against the attack roll; succeed and the hit is negated. Riposte: when an enemy misses you in melee, make a free attack against it. Acrobatic Escape: when hit, a Dexterity check against the attack roll; succeed to halve the damage and move 20ft (kit) without provoking. No Parry with a shield or in medium or heavy armour.

Finesse. Dexterity for attack and damage with light or finesse melee weapons.

Agile Defence. +2 AC in light armour or none, with no shield (included).

Opening Flourish. Your first hit each encounter adds your Charisma modifier (+2) to damage.

Duel's Rhythm. While in melee with a single opponent and no one else in reach, Advantage on your first attack roll each round and on saves.

Light Feet. Creatures you attacked this turn can't make Attacks of Opportunity as you move away.

Hit and Run. On a turn you attack, +10ft speed, and once a round you may move through one enemy's space without provoking Attacks of Opportunity.

En Garde. Advantage on initiative rolls.

Relentless Assault. Each hit after the first on the same target in a round adds +1d4 damage.

Extra Attack. When you use your action to attack, make one more weapon attack, with Disadvantage.

Disarming Strike. On a hit, instead of dealing damage, the target makes a Fortitude save (DC 18) or drops what it holds. It counts as your attack for that round.

Flèche. 4 times a day, as part of your action, lunge for one more melee attack, with Disadvantage.

Kit: Deckhand's Escape. Acrobatic Escape moves you 20ft, on any terrain without penalty.

Kit: Dockside Rapport. Advantage on Seamanship checks and on Charisma checks with sailors, dock workers and maritime merchants.

Half-Elf. Low-light vision. Immune to magical sleep; Advantage on saves against charm and on social checks with humans and elves. Fully rested after a 4-hour trance or 8 hours' sleep. Knack: Advantage on Etiquette checks.

Dual Heritage. Once a day, reroll one failed save or check (1 Luck for a second use).

Two-Weapon Fighting (1st, Specialist). Your off-hand attack has no Disadvantage.

Swift Reflexes (2nd, General). +1 Dexterity (included) and Advantage on initiative.

Toughness (6th, General). +1 HP per level and +1 Constitution (both included); Advantage on Constitution checks.

HP. 1st level: d8 max 8 + Con 1 = 9. Levels 2 to 9: 8 x (5 + 1) = 48. Toughness: 9. Total 66.

Armour Class on the sheet: 10 + 4 (Studded Leather +1) + 4 (Dex) + 2 (Agile Defence, light armour and no shield) = 20

Class Abilities

1st Level

Finesse

  • Effect: A reminder of the Finesse weapon trait, which this class extends to light melee weapons: use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with light or finesse melee weapons (rapier, dagger, main gauche, short sword).

Agile Defence

  • Effect: +1 AC while wearing light armour or no armour and carrying no shield. Does not stack with other unarmoured bonuses of the same kind.
  • An additional +1 at 7th, 13th, and 19th levels
  • AC bonus by level: +2 total at 7th, +3 at 13th, +4 at 19th.

Opening Flourish

  • Effect: Your first hit in each encounter adds your Charisma modifier as a flat bonus to damage. Always on: the psychological edge of style is a genuine weapon.

Flourish Manoeuvres

  • Effect: The Swashbuckler's reactive tricks — Parry, Riposte, and later additions — all draw from the same well.
  • Once per round, out of turn, perform one Flourish Manoeuvre from those currently known.
  • Using one manoeuvre in a round means none of the others are available until the next round.
  • Known at 1st level — Parry: when struck in melee, make a Dexterity check (d20 + Dexterity modifier) against the attacker's attack roll. On success, negate the hit entirely. Cannot use while wearing medium or heavy armour or while carrying a shield

2nd Level

Duel's Rhythm

  • Effect: While engaged with a single opponent in melee (no other creatures in melee reach), gain advantage on your first attack roll each round and on saves.

3rd Level

  • Flourish Manoeuvres gains a new option — Riposte: when an enemy misses you with a melee attack, immediately make a free attack against them as though it were your Flourish Manoeuvre for the round

4th Level

Light Feet

  • Effect: Creatures you have attacked this turn cannot make opportunity attacks against you as you move away.

Hit and Run

  • Effect: On a turn you make an attack, your speed increases by 10ft (20ft from 13th level). Once per round, you can move through one enemy's space. Moving through that space doesn't provoke Attacks of Opportunity.

5th Level

En Garde

  • Effect: Advantage on all initiative rolls.

6th Level

Relentless Assault

  • Effect: Each successful hit after the first against the same target in a single round adds flat +1d4 damage (not cumulative). Resets at the start of the next round.

7th Level

Disarming Strike

  • Effect: On a hit, instead of dealing damage, force the target to make a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC, or drop whatever they are holding. Counts as the attack for that round.

Extra Attack

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).

8th Level

Flèche

  • Effect: As part of your action on your turn, lunge for a second strike — make one additional melee attack this round, usable a number of times per day equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum 1/day). This is an extra attack, rolled with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).
  • This is the reliable way to feed Relentless Assault a second hit without waiting on an enemy to miss — Riposte and Perfect Parry still work too, and all three can set up the same round's stacking bonus.

9th Level

  • Flourish Manoeuvres gains a new option — Acrobatic Escape: when hit, make a Dexterity check (d20 + Dexterity modifier) against the attacker's attack roll. On success, halve the incoming damage and move up to 10ft without triggering opportunity attacks

10th Level

Master Duelist

  • Effect: Once per day, declare a decisive strike. Make one melee attack — if it hits, it deals maximum damage automatically. A miss still uses it.
  • Any creature of lower Level that witnesses this strike must make a Will save against your Class Save DC, or suffer disadvantage on their first attack against the Swashbuckler in any future combat where they recognise them

13th Level

Perfect Parry

  • Effect: The Parry option within Flourish Manoeuvres now succeeds automatically on a natural 16+ on the Dexterity check, without needing to meet or beat the attack roll.
  • A successful Perfect Parry (not just a normal Parry) triggers a free Riposte immediately — this Riposte does not cost the round's Flourish Manoeuvre, since the parry itself was the manoeuvre spent

15th Level

  • Dexterity Bonus: permanent +1 Dexterity

16th Level

Second Flourish

  • Effect: You may perform two Flourish Manoeuvres each round instead of one, both out of turn.

24th Level

Master Duelist (Improved)

  • Effect: Master Duelist can be used once per encounter instead of once per day.

Kits: Duelling Schools of Arneyan

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Swashbuckler folder. Drag one onto your character.

Swashbuckler Kits represent the fencing school or street tradition that shaped the character's blade.

system.description:
Two blades moving independently is supposed to get you killed — one always lagging half a beat behind the other.

  • You've closed that gap; both hands work like they belong to the same fight.
  • Your off-hand attack no longer suffers Disadvantage.
  • The same feat as in the Martial Path; you can only take it once.

Available to: Rogues, Assassins, Rangers, Monks, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, and Artificers.
